en.d: A module is a course your coaches complete — made of units, which are made of lessons. Everything in this guide lives in the left-hand menu of Club Settings. Start by clicking "Modules".
Click "Create Module". Your work is saved as a draft automatically while you build.
Give it a clear title and a short description. You can credit a coach, and keep the status "Unpublished" until it's ready.
Upload a cover image (SVG, PNG or JPG), optionally award a certificate, and set CPD points — by default they total up automatically from each unit.
In the Units section, click "Create Unit" to open the unit builder.

Give the unit its own CPD points and estimated duration. Optionally add a time limit, or enable "Free navigation" so coaches can move between lessons in any order — otherwise they complete them in sequence.

en.t: Build lessons from six content types
en.d: Add lessons, then fill each one with items: Question, Video, Article, PDF, External Video or SCORM. A typical lesson is a video followed by a question.

en.t: Set the pass mark and save
en.d: Use "Percentage To Pass" to set how much of the unit a coach must complete, then click "Create Unit". You can Preview it first, exactly as a coach would see it.

en.t: Your module is built — now get it in front of coaches
en.d: Publishing a module doesn't make it visible on its own. Coaches see content through Content Rails — themed rows shown together under one title. Back in the left menu, click "Content Rails".
Click "Create Content Rail" — or reuse an existing one if you already have a home for this kind of content.
Give the rail a clear title and description — coaches won't see the description, it's just for your reference. An image is optional.
Click "Create". The rail starts as Unpublished — you'll add your module and publish it next.

en.t: Add your module as an activity
en.d: On the "Activities" tab, click "Add Activity" and choose "Module" — you can also add Events, Exams, or even another Rail nested inside this one.
Search by name and tick the module you just built. You can select several at once if you're adding more than one.
Click "Add" to bring the selected items into the rail.

en.t: Your module now lives on the rail
en.d: Each item shows its type and status. Drag the handle on the left to reorder them, or click "Add Activity" again any time to add more.
Back on the "Details" tab, change Status to "Published", then click "Update" to save.

en.t: One last step — put the rail on the page
en.d: A published rail still needs a home. In the same left menu, click "Page Builder" — this is where the coach homepage is built.
You'll usually have just one page, called "My Learning Content". Click it to edit what coaches see.
Hover over any row in the Content list — a "+" appears on the right. Click it. The new block lands directly below the row you hovered.
You can add a Paragraph, Header, List, Image or Divider too — but to show your content, pick "Rail".
Search by name if the list is long, then tick the rail you just published. Only published rails will show to coaches.
Click "Add" to drop the rail into the page.

en.t: Put it in the right order
en.d: The order here is the order coaches see. Use the handle on the right of any row to move it up or down — top of the list means top of their homepage.
Click "Update". Nothing changes for coaches until you do.

en.t: That's it — your content is live
en.d: Your rail now sits on the coach homepage, with everything you added inside it.

en.doneD: You've built a module, published it through a rail, and placed that rail on the coach homepage. Repeat the last section any time you want to add, reorder or remove a row — and remember nothing changes for coaches until you click Update.
en.lead: For club admins. Build your own modules — units, lessons, videos, questions, even SCORM — then publish them to coaches and put them on the homepage.
